authors: Aggarwal S; Jeong D; Kumar N; Park DS; Robinson J; Spearot A
title: COVID-19 market disruptions and food security: Evidence from households in rural Liberia and Malawi
verification: Crossref metadata verified; S1 Data downloaded and hash-verified; replication do-file read (attrition tables S1-S3, HHS usage). Article full text not re-read in this session.
population_data: Rural Liberia and Malawi; control households of cash-transfer RCT; bimonthly household phone survey 2020-2021 (Malawi from Jul 2019)
outcome_indicator: HDDS, FCS, HHS (z-scored indices); expenditures; prices
estimand_or_target: Mean changes in food security relative to Jan-Feb 2020 during COVID-19 market disruptions
methods: Household fixed-effects event-study regressions; crop-vendor price panel
main_finding: Food security worsened in early pandemic months, partly recovering; market disruptions documented
authors_limitations: Attrition from phone panel (Appendix Tables S1-S3); control-only sample
our_critique: Source of our data; studies mean outcomes, not household ascertainment
incremental_value_of_this_study: New estimand (household ascertainment under thinned schedules), bounds, timing test; no overlap in question

authors: Aggarwal S; Aker J; Jeong D; Kumar N; Park DS; Robinson J; Spearot A
title: The Dynamic Effects of Cash Transfers to Agricultural Households
verification: Crossref metadata + OpenAlex abstract verified; full text not accessed (paywall)

authors: Bell A; Ward P; Tamal M; Killilea M
title: Assessing recall bias and measurement error in high-frequency social data collection for human-environment research
population_data: ~500 farmers, rural Bangladesh; smartphone (ODK) survey tasks
outcome_indicator: Consumption, experience (e.g. sick days), labour/time-use recall
methods: Randomised task frequency: weekly, monthly or seasonal
main_finding: Recall of consumption and experiences decays much more than recall of labour/farm time use
our_critique: Relevant to our 'retrospective thinning is not prospective sparse design' caveat
incremental_value_of_this_study: We hold recall fixed (30 days) and only thin windows; Bell et al. show real frequency changes may alter responses, which we cannot model

authors: Livings MS; Bruine de Bruin W; Wilson JP; Lee BY; Xu M; Frazzini A; Chandra S; Weber K
title: Food Insecurity Is Under-reported in Surveys That Ask About the Past Year
verification: Crossref metadata verified; finding summarised from search-result abstract text (abstract-level)
estimand_or_target: Agreement between repeated past-week reports and an annual past-year report
main_finding: About one-third of people reporting past-week FI during 2021 did not report past-year FI in Dec 2021
our_critique: Different setting (US) and different mechanism (long recall)
overlap_with_this_study: Repeated short-recall measurement detects more affected people than infrequent measurement
incremental_value_of_this_study: We quantify the frequency frontier for a fixed short recall rather than recall-period under-reporting

authors: Nord M; Andrews M; Winicki J
title: Frequency and Duration of Food Insecurity and Hunger in US Households
venue: Journal of Nutrition Education and Behavior 34(4):194-201
verification: Crossref metadata verified; content via National Academies summary (secondary)
estimand_or_target: Monthly vs annual prevalence; recurrence and duration
main_finding: Monthly prevalence of hunger ~60% of annual prevalence; episodes are recurrent but not chronic
our_critique: Early evidence that point-in-time measures understate ever-affected households

title: Food security dynamics and measurement error
population_data: US Panel Study of Income Dynamics (PSID)
estimand_or_target: Intra- and intergenerational food-security transition matrices under measurement error
methods: Partial identification of transition matrices under misclassification
main_finding: Even modest measurement error can dwarf information in the data; much is learned under weak assumptions (serially uncorrelated errors most informative); persistence in the tails
our_critique: Closest methodological relative for misclassification-robust bounds; must be read in full before submission
overlap_with_this_study: Partial identification of food-security dynamics under measurement error
incremental_value_of_this_study: Our bounds target a different functional (ascertainment ratio under thinning) with a shared flip budget; cite as methodological precedent, do not claim novelty of bounding

authors: Zhu H; Gupta A; Doan MK; Michuda A
title: Misidentified household food insecurity: how relying on a single survey round produces targeting errors in food security programs
verification: FULL TEXT read (open access, CC BY 4.0; PDF retrieved and text-extracted)
population_data: 305 households, Sundarbans, West Bengal, India; weekly financial diaries Nov 2018-Oct 2019 (50 weeks)
outcome_indicator: Expenditure-derived MEB, food expenditure share, FCS constructed from expenditure
estimand_or_target: Misclassification of a single random week vs household annual-average classification
methods: Monte Carlo resampling of single weeks (10,000 reps); lagged recall modules; multi-indicator combination (PCA/factor)
main_finding: Single-round misclassification 15-48% depending on indicator; combining indicators reduces to ~6-15%
authors_limitations: Annual average as benchmark; FCS constructed from expenditures; single region
our_critique: Closest prior work. Benchmark is annual average status, not ever-positive ascertainment; indicators are expenditure-based, not experiential HHS; no attrition/missing-data bounds; no out-of-year test
overlap_with_this_study: SAME CORE MESSAGE: single/infrequent measurement misidentifies households because food security fluctuates; repeated measurement reduces errors
incremental_value_of_this_study: HHS (experiential, 30-day), explicit ever-positive ascertainment estimand, full frequency frontier m=1..6, sharp missing-data and label-error bounds, frozen out-of-year calendar test, two African countries with village clustering. Increment is real but modest

authors: Na M; Caswell BL; Talegawkar SA; Palmer A
title: Monthly food insecurity assessment in rural mkushi district, Zambia: a longitudinal analysis
population_data: 157 rural households, Mkushi, Zambia; 6 monthly visits Oct 2012-Mar 2013
estimand_or_target: Within- vs between-household variance of monthly HFI
main_finding: Within-household variance (10.6) exceeded between (8.8); repeated assessments may be needed to avoid household-level misclassification
overlap_with_this_study: Monthly repeated HFI; household-level misclassification concern
incremental_value_of_this_study: We quantify how many reference-positive households are missed per number of screens, with bounds and timing test
